Reproducibility: not applicable. as a new capability. The related predecessor does provide high-confidence live reproduction of the unsafe old controller lookup blocking Messages.app.

target.title: feat: add Messages Name & Photo sharing
target.body:
## Summary

- supersedes #166 and builds on @omarshahine's implementation, fail-closed runtime proof, and bridge-liveness finding
- fixes the existing nickname lookup to use the current `IMNicknameController` singleton and an `IMHandle`
- adds canonical `imsg name-photo status|share` commands plus the BlueBubbles-compatible bridge actions and Photon-compatible RPC method names
- uses the verified Name & Photo selector family, chat participants, and a chat-bound local sender identity; privacy-sensitive sharing fails closed when those cannot be proven
- reports request submission rather than claiming delivery, and documents the explicit-consent requirement

The watcher change from #166 is intentionally not included. It deserves a separate measured fix instead of adding another polling timer to the injected helper.

## Validation

- `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer make test` — 209 tests passed
- `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer make lint` — passed; 9 existing non-serious warnings
- `make build-dylib` — passed
- signed arm64 CLI plus arm64/arm64e helper build — passed strict code-sign verification
- source-blind CLI validation — 4 passed, 0 failed, 1 live bridge clause blocked by host SIP
- pre-commit review plus current runtime/decompile verification — complete
- GitHub CI — macOS and Linux read-core jobs passed

## Live proof

The repository, selector, compile, and executable-level proof is complete. Receiver-visible current-head proof remains pending because the prepared SIP-off macOS VM still needs a one-time Apple Account / Messages sign-in. This is a draft until that proof is available; no profile share was sent during validation.

## Credit

This replacement preserves Omar's authorship in the commit trailer and thanks @omarshahine in the changelog. I should have separated the useful feature direction and runtime findings from the patch-shape problems before closing #166.
